scenes.title: 1961 Caltech Discrimination Box: Shifting a Soft Eye-Patch Resets an Articulated Porcelain Cat's 100% 'Circle vs Cross' Mastery Back to Zero

layout.description: Sunlit high-key 1961 Caltech neurobiology laboratory featuring a clean white wooden two-choice **Visual Discrimination Box** displaying two illuminated translucent push-panels (**Circle [+]** vs **Cross [-]**), an **articulated matte-white porcelain cat sculpture** wearing a tiny reversible soft white felt monocle eye-shield, and Roger Sperry's twin learning-curve board ('Right Eye: 100% Mastered -> Swap Patch to Left Eye: 50% Naive Reset!').

positions.who: Roger Sperry (mannequin in crisp 1961 white lab coat over slim tie)
positions.where: standing beside the discrimination box gently shifting the tiny reversible white felt eye-shield from the porcelain cat's left side to its right side while pointing to the vertical drop on the learning chart

confidently pressing the illuminated **Circle** panel with its paw under Eye 1 (100% accuracy), then hesitating equally between Circle and Cross as a complete novice the moment the eye-shield switches to Eye 2

props.name: illuminated two-choice 'Circle (+) vs Cross (-)' push-panel box
props.physical_behavior: stages Sperry's exact 1961 Science visual discrimination

props.name: articulated matte-white porcelain cat sculpture with reversible felt eye-shield
props.period_detail: cleanly visualizes single-eye hemisphere routing under R46 porcelain animal aesthetics
props.physical_behavior: makes the eye-swap reset crystal clear

props.name: Intact Callosum (100% Transfer) vs Split Callosum (50% Reset) dual-curve board
props.period_detail: shows why Control Group 1 remembered instantly while Split Group 2 started over from scratch
props.physical_behavior: proves the exact job of 200 million callosal fibers

actions.verb_sequence: presses the Circle (+) panel briskly 10/10 times with Right Eye open -> Roger Sperry gently swaps the soft felt shield to uncover ONLY the Left Eye -> porcelain cat pauses undecided between Circle and Cross at 50% chance

reactions.reaction: mark the sharp vertical drop from 100% down to 50% naive baseline on Trial 1 of the second eye

scenes.wardrobe: 1961 California laboratory attire: crisp white cotton lab coat, slim dark tie, short-sleeve dress shirt.
scenes.recognition_hook: With the left eye covered, it nails 'Circle over Cross' ten times out of ten — move the eye-patch two centimetres to the other eye and its brain has never seen a circle in its life!

key_visual.description: a 1961 Caltech lab table with a two-panel Circle-versus-Cross discrimination box, an articulated matte-white porcelain cat sculpture with a reversible eye shield, and a 100%-to-50% transfer graph

scenes.title: Polarized Filters: Teaching Opposite Rules to Left & Right Brains at Once!

layout.description: Bright optical bench where opposite polarized lenses project 'Circle = Reward' to the Left Hemisphere and 'Cross = Reward' to the Right Hemisphere simultaneously.

positions.where: rotating polarized filter slides to show two opposite habits coexisting inside one skull without interference

props.name: crossed polarizing filter paddles & split Circle/Cross scorecards
props.period_detail: proves two independent memory systems can store contradictory truths simultaneously

actions.verb_sequence: flips Left polarizer ('Pushes Circle!') -> flips Right polarizer ('Pushes Cross!')

reactions.reaction: stares amazed planning the first human split-brain tests

scenes.recognition_hook: Using polarized lenses, Sperry taught one hemisphere 'Circle wins, Cross loses' and the OTHER hemisphere 'Cross wins, Circle loses' on the exact same afternoon!
